fields.doc: Raise to play, lower to stop. The engine lowers it when a non-looping clip ends.
Clip completed (runtime, read-only). Raise Playing to play it again.
Side of the square atlas, in texels.
How finely a surface is lit. A world unit is a design pixel.
How many times light may reflect. 0 = direct only.
Rays each lumel gathers per bounce.
Directions each probe gathers, over the whole sphere.
Fingerprint of the inputs the last bake read.
Last root status (runtime, read-only).
Parallax scroll factor (1 = with world, <1 = slower, 0 = locked to camera).
Radius of the disc on the ground, in world units.
How dark the disc is at its centre.
How soft its edge is (0 hard, 1 fading from the centre).
Height of the flat ground. A ground function set from code overrides it.
Height above the ground at which the shadow is gone (0 never fades it).
How small the disc gets at that height (0 keeps its size).
How far above the ground the disc is drawn.
Orthographic (2D) or Perspective projection.
Half the visible height in world units (Orthographic).
Which buffers to clear before rendering this camera.
Snap the camera to the pixel grid for crisp pixel-art (Orthographic).
Which sorting layers this camera renders.
Render into a RenderTexture instead of the screen (0 = screen). Set at run time.
Draw this camera's whole view volume in the editor, not just what it frames on the content plane.
World pixels per physics meter (Box2D + tile collider scale).
How the canvas adapts the design resolution to the screen.
0 matches width, 1 matches height (Match mode only).
Sorting layer this UI belongs to — cameras cull by it.
Max walkable slope from up (radians)
Floor-snap probe length; 0 disables stair/slope stick
Steepest ground it can stand on
How hard it can shove what it walks into
Width and height of the content in local units (before scale).
The point of the rectangle the entity sits on, as a fraction of its size (0.5,0.5 = centre). Rotation and scale turn about it.
Geometry (.esmesh) whose convex hull collides.
The sprite's alpha, as a share of its own, while something stands under it.
Seconds the fade takes, either way.
Ground around the sprite's edge that counts as under it, in world units.
The covered ground is the ellipse inside the sprite's rectangle (a tree crown) and not the whole of it (a roof).
How squarely a surface must face the projector to take the decal.
What the last cut read.
Where the joint attaches on the connected body, in that body's frame (pixels).
Where it attaches on this entity, in its own frame (pixels).
Whether this entity can be dragged at all.
Pointer travel before a press becomes a drag.
Pin the X axis; the drag only moves in Y.
Pin the Y axis; the drag only moves in X.
Apply the lower bound below.
Lowest world position the drag may reach.
Apply the upper bound below.
Highest world position the drag may reach.
Where the joint attaches on the connected body, in that body's frame (pixels).
Where it attaches on this entity, in its own frame (pixels).
The water's density against the body's. 1 holds it up exactly when it is wholly under; 2 floats it half under.
How hard the water resists the body moving through it, per second.
How deep under the surface, in world units, a point of the body is wholly wet.
Points of the body, in its own space, the water is asked about: spread them (the corners of a hull) and waves tip it. Empty is the one at its origin.
How much of a ripple the body makes in water that keeps ripples (WaterZone Ripples). 0 makes none.
The world rectangle the fog covers, centred on this entity.
The world rectangle the fog covers, centred on this entity.
How many texels a side the maps are: finer edges, and more to paint.
How far a viewer with no radius of its own sees.
How many rays are cast from each viewer: the fineness of the field of view's edge.
The plant to scatter. Empty grows grass.
A material on the Foliage shader, which makes the wind. Empty draws the plants still, in their own colours.
World size along x, centred on this entity.
World size along z, centred on this entity.
Side of the cells the area is cut into. Each is one mesh, culled whole.
Plants per cell.
Another seed grows the same plants in other places.
The least a place may face up and still grow something. Lower lets plants onto slopes.
The lowest world height plants grow at.
The highest world height plants grow at.
How deep under water a plant may stand. 0 keeps them on dry ground; reeds stand in the shallows.
Height of a blade at scale 1.
Width of a blade at its base, at scale 1.
Past this a cell is drawn as its far version: fewer, broader blades, or a tree as crossed cards.
Past this a cell is not drawn.
The part of the plant's texture a far tree shows (left, bottom, right, top).
The outline of the cards a far tree is drawn as.
How far it travels between two steps.
How far apart the left and right feet are.
A footprint's length.
How long a footprint lasts before it has faded.
A ring's width when it has spread.
How long a ring takes to spread and fade.
The sprite layer the steps are drawn on: above the ground, below whatever walks.
Also leave a print where there is no StepSurface.
Opacity of this entity and everything under it, multiplied with the opacity of every group above it.
Where the joint attaches on the connected body, in that body's frame (pixels).
Where it attaches on this entity, in its own frame (pixels).
Where the joint attaches, in THIS entity's frame (world units).
How close it gets before it swings.
Geometry drawn below the LOD 1 screen size.
Geometry drawn below the LOD 2 screen size.
Geometry drawn below the LOD 3 screen size.
Screen height fraction below which LOD 1 takes over.
Screen height fraction below which LOD 2 takes over.
Screen height fraction below which LOD 3 takes over.
Screen height fraction below which nothing is drawn (0 = never).
Extra fraction to grow past a threshold before the finer level returns.
Off: the MeshRenderer's own mesh is always drawn.
Point, Directional, Ambient, or Spot.
Brightness multiplier of the light.
Falloff reach in world units (Point / Spot).
Radius held at full strength before the falloff starts.
Falloff shape: 1 = linear, higher pools near the light, lower reaches further.
How much of this light its shadows remove (1 = all of it).
The lowest sprite layer this light reaches (default: every layer).
The highest sprite layer this light reaches (default: every layer).
A texture whose alpha shapes this light (a cookie).
Cookie size in world units; 0 = the light's own reach.
Shadow softness (light-source size); 0 = hard edge.
Angular size of a Directional light's source (the sun is 0.53); 0 = hard edge.
Directional shadow distance; 0 = no directional shadow.
Cast a shadow map over 3D meshes (Directional, Spot, Point).
Shadow map coverage radius; 0 = fit the view.
Take direction and strength from the environment's sun, and light the sky without it.
With Follow Environment Sun: aim by this light's Transform, not by the panorama.
Baked environment (.esenv) this Ambient light casts.
Turn the environment about the up axis, in degrees.
Draw this environment as the sky behind the scene.
Scale what baked reflection probes show (1 = as baked).
How much colour baked reflection probes keep (0 = grey).
Multiply baked indirect light (lightmaps, probe volumes) by this colour (1 = as baked).
Baked probe grid (.esprobes) filling this box.
Half the box this volume covers, from the entity's position.
World units between probes the next bake lays down.
The animated socket the swing reaches from.
Geometry (.esmesh) to collide against.
The cheaper mesh used past the LOD distance. Needs the same channels as the mesh.
Distance (metres) past which the cheaper mesh is used. 0 = never.
Distance (metres) nearer than which an instance is not drawn. 0 = from the eye.
Distance (metres) past which an instance is not drawn. 0 = unlimited.
Distance (metres) past which an instance casts no shadow. 0 = as far as it is drawn.
Baked lightmap atlas. Needs a mesh with a second UV set.
Atlas rectangle: xy scales the second UV set, zw offsets it.
Weight per morph target of the mesh, in the order the mesh carries them.
Normal map (tangent space). Needs a mesh with normals.
Tint multiplied into the vertex colors (white = unchanged).
Sorting layer — controls draw order across renderables.
Opaque: no blending; writes and tests depth, so meshes occlude each other.
Cull back faces: triangles facing away from the camera are skipped.
Receive 2D lights: Light entities light this mesh (flat normal). A custom material overrides this.
Cast shadows: whether this mesh blocks the light. Water and other surfaces light passes through say no.
Parallax scroll factor (1 = with world, <1 = slower, 0 = locked to camera).
Joint entities, in the order the mesh's bind matrices are in.
Periodic replan cadence; 0 disables periodic refresh. Targets, obstacles and blocked-route recovery still replan.
What crossing it costs against 1 for open ground.
Whether it can be taken both ways — a drop off a ledge cannot.
How far from each end ground may be and still be joined.
Whether it blocks right now — a door that opens.
Vertical voxel size; what separates one level from the one above it.
Headroom an agent needs to walk somewhere.
How wide the agent is; the mesh is pulled back from walls by this.
Layer mask the ground is taken from; 0 = every layer.
Half the solid box, in world units, from the entity's position.
Off: this box hides nothing.
How fast this emitter's own time runs: 2 plays it twice as fast, 0.5 at half, 0 holds it. Scales emission, lifetimes and motion alike.
Seconds after the emitter starts playing before it emits anything. The duration counts from the end of the delay.
Simulate on the GPU (WebGPU compute). Falls back to a capped CPU simulation elsewhere. Sub-emitters, trails and physics collision are CPU-only.
A velocity each particle carries on top of its own, chosen between the two ends when it is born. Gravity, damping, noise and the speed limit do not act on it. Run by the CPU simulation.
The fastest a particle may move under its own velocity; 0 is no limit. A faster particle is pulled back toward the limit. Run by the CPU simulation.
How much of the excess over the limit is removed per 1/60 s: 1 clamps at once, a small value brakes gently.

Billboard faces the view. Stretched lays the quad's long axis (its Y) along the particle's velocity and lengthens it with speed. Drawn by the CPU simulation; a GPU-simulated emitter draws as Billboard.
Stretched: how much of the particle's speed is added to the quad's length, in world units per unit of speed.
Stretched: the quad's own length is its size times this.
'x' is screen-right (a flat scene); '-z' is where an imported model faces.
3D layer mask the sight ray may hit; 0 = every layer.
A target is seen (runtime, read-only).
World size along x, centred on this entity.
World size along z, centred on this entity.
Side of the cells the area is cut into. Each kind in a cell is one mesh a part, culled whole.
What each kind of plant is made of: its parts (mesh, cheaper mesh, material, texture, tint) and how far it is drawn.
Where each plant stands: kind index, x, y, z, turn about the vertical in radians and scale, six numbers a plant, in this entity's space.
Local normal axis, transformed with the entity. Y for a floor, Z for a mirror.
Clip offset in world units; excludes geometry behind the reflecting plane.
Sorting-layer bits captured by the reflection. The receiving surface and screen UI are excluded.
Only the reflection capture; never limits the main scene frame rate.
The planet's radius in metres. The planet stands at its entity, unrotated and unscaled.
The generator the ground is made by, registered with registerPlanetProvider. The same provider, world, seed and version are the same ground everywhere.
The world (a planet) the ground belongs to, as the game names it; handed to the provider.
The generator version the planet was made with. A version the provider no longer has fails the planet rather than growing other ground under what was built on it.
Another seed is another planet.
The finest cell of the ground's mesh, in metres: what it is drawn at near the eye. Further off the cells double, level by level.
Above 1 the finest cells reach further out before the ground coarsens.
The size, in metres, of the ground's own wander in brightness.
How strongly the ground's brightness wanders.
Whether 3D bodies and characters collide with the ground: the finest tiles round each of them are built as collision geometry.
How far round each moving body and character the ground is built for collision, in metres.
The collision layer the ground is in (0 to 15).
The ground's friction.
How hard the planet pulls bodies toward its centre, in metres a second squared at the surface (9.81 is the Earth's). Needs 3D physics; the world's own gravity is taken off the bodies it pulls.
Whether the planet has a sea: a sphere at the sea level, in which the ground that dips below it stands.
The height of the sea above the planet's radius, in metres.
How much of the sea there is over what is under it.
The terrain layers (.esterrainlayer, up to four) the ground is drawn with, in the order the paint weighs them, each read on the planes of the world's axes. Empty draws the four layer colours.
Where the joint attaches, in THIS entity's frame (world units).
The covered ground is the ellipse inside the sprite's rectangle (a tree crown) and not the whole of it (a roof).
Ground around the sprite's edge that stays dry too, in world units.
Ground around the sprite's edge that the rain still draws on, in world units: the feet, or a trunk's base.
The scene's baked reflections (the baker writes this).
Half the box this probe answers inside, from the entity's position.
Which column of the atlas this probe occupies (the baker writes this).
Off: what stands inside this box reflects the sky again.
Check the whole path a step covers — what a bullet needs
Occluder box size in world units (centred on the entity, turning with it). Unused when the caster has an outline.
Parallax scroll factor (1 = with world, <1 = slower, 0 = locked to camera).
The sprite's alpha, as a share of its own, while no viewer sees it.
Seconds the fade takes, either way.
How far this eye sees. 0 is no limit: only a wall stops it.
Attachment in this entity’s local frame, in world units.
Local X/twist direction. Must be nonzero.
Local Y reference. Must not be parallel to the X/twist axis.
Body B relative to A, in constraint axes (rad/s).
Maximum torque per motor axis (N m).
Each axis: 0 locked, 1 limited, 2 free.
Each axis: 0 locked, 1 limited, 2 free.
Body B relative to A, in constraint axes (world units/s).
Maximum force per translation axis (N).
Where the joint attaches on the connected body, in that body's frame (pixels).
Where it attaches on this entity, in its own frame (pixels).
Direction of travel, in the connected body's frame.
Where the joint attaches, in THIS entity's frame (world units).
Sorting layer for the entire group — members no longer state their own.
Draw order of the whole group inside its sorting layer — higher draws on top.
Fixed 32-bit seed for this source selection stream.
The points the curve passes through, in order, in the entity's own space. Each carries the width of whatever follows the curve there.
Join the end of the curve to its start (three points or more).
Off leaves the chain exactly as the animation poses it.
How hard each bone is pulled back toward its animated pose. 0 hangs free, 1 follows the animation exactly.
How much of its speed a bone loses each frame. Higher settles sooner.
Gravity on the chain, in world units a second squared (world y is up).
A steady wind on the chain, in world units a second squared. Zero is still air.
How far gusts swing the wind's strength. 0 is a steady wind, 1 takes it from calm to twice its strength.
Gusts a second.
Length of the tip past each end bone, in world units. 0 leaves the end bones unsimulated.
Thickness of the strand, in world units, kept clear of the colliders.
How much of the simulation is used. 0 is the animation alone.
Entities with a SpringBoneCollider that this chain is kept out of (the head, the shoulders).
Sphere, or a capsule along the entity's own Y axis.
Radius in world units, before the entity's scale.
A capsule's length between the centres of its end spheres, in world units before scale.
Where the centre of the shape is, in the entity's own space.
Tint multiplied into the texture (white = unchanged).
Anchor point the sprite rotates and scales about, as a fraction of its size (0.5,0.5 = centre). Values outside 0–1 sit off the sprite.
Sorting layer — controls draw order across sprites.
Draw order inside the sorting layer — higher draws on top. Overrides the layer's Y-sort or depth ordering; leave 0 to keep it.
Whether a SpriteMask drawn before this sprite clips it, and which side survives.
Receive 2D lights: Light entities light this sprite (flat normal). A custom material overrides this.
Draw mode: Auto infers from tile size and the texture's 9-slice border; the others override it.
Parallax scroll factor (1 = with world, <1 = slower, 0 = locked to camera).
Cut to the sprite's shape instead of its box: fragments below this alpha do not mask.
Limit how far this mask reaches; off = every sprite drawn after it.
Last sorting layer this mask reaches.
Last order inside that layer this mask reaches, inclusive.
Active state (runtime, read-only).
Meshes batch only with others of the same group. Empty is the default group.

values: Not merged: alone in its group

fields.doc: What a step on this ground leaves: a ring that spreads, or a footprint.
The covered ground is the ellipse inside the sprite's rectangle and not the whole of it.
Ground around the sprite's edge that counts as on it, in world units.
Edge of one cell on the plane.
Which two world axes the cells are cut along: a 3D world is cut on the ground, a 2D world on the screen plane.
How far from the entity the plants lean away.
How hard they lean: 1 is the full lean the material's Push Strength says.
Attachment in this entity’s local frame, in world units.
Local X/twist direction. Must be nonzero.
Local Y reference. Must not be parallel to the X/twist axis.
Body B relative to A, in constraint axes (rad/s).
Maximum torque per motor axis (N m).
An area of its own size, from a heightmap or noise; or ground that goes on for ever, from noise read anywhere (the same seed is the same ground).

The generator the ground is made by, without end or (with no heightmap) in an area: estella:noise, or one the game registers. The same provider, world, seed and version are the same ground on every machine, and two areas side by side join.
The world (a planet, a level) the ground belongs to, as the game names it; handed to the provider.
The generator version the world was made with. A version the provider no longer has fails the terrain rather than growing other ground under what was built.
A heightmap image, read as data (shipped as the PNG it is). Empty makes the ground from noise; a heightmap that cannot be read fails the terrain instead.
How the heightmap holds its heights: grey (or red) at the depth of the file, 16 bits from a 16-bit PNG; or sixteen bits across red (high byte) and green (low byte) of an 8-bit image.
An image whose red, green, blue and alpha are the weights of grass, dirt, snow and rock.
An image whose red, green, blue and alpha are the weights of layers 5 to 8.
The terrain layers (.esterrainlayer, up to eight) the ground is drawn with, in the order the paint weighs them. Empty draws the four layer colours.
A material on the Terrain shader (on Terrain Layers when the ground has layers). Empty uses the stock one.
An area's size along x; for ground without end, the span its hills are spread over.
An area's size along z.
World height of the highest ground.
The finest cell of the ground's mesh, in world units: what it is drawn at near the eye. Further off the cells double, level by level.
Above 1 the finest cells reach further out before the ground coarsens.
How far ground without end is drawn.
Whether 3D bodies and characters collide with the ground: the finest level's triangles, wherever the camera is.
How far round each moving body and character the ground is built for collision, in world units.
The collision layer the ground is in (0 to 15).
How much the ground holds what slides on it.
Another seed is another ground.
How many hills across the terrain (or across sizeX, for ground without end).
Layers of detail in the noise.
How much of its height each finer layer keeps. Lower is smoother.
0 is rolling hills; 1 is sharp ridges.
Samples along each side of an area's noise ground.
How far the noise is bent by noise of its own: winding valleys and bent ridges instead of round hills.
How much rain wears the ground: an area (a heightmap's too) drop by drop, with dirt where the water ran; ground without end by its noise. 0 leaves it as made.
How steep ground must be to turn to rock. 0 is flat, 1 is sheer.
The height, as a share of the terrain, where grass gives way to dirt.
The height, as a share of the terrain, where snow begins.
Localization key — when set, content is resolved from the Localization catalogs (and re-resolved on locale switch). Leave empty for plain text.
A font file this project ships (.ttf / .otf). Overrides Font Family when set; leave empty to use a font the host already has.
A font the HOST already has (system or page-loaded). Ignored when Font is set.
Horizontal alignment: within the layout box when the entity has a UINode, else it anchors the text to the entity origin (left/center/right edge).
Vertical alignment: within the layout box when the entity has a UINode, else it anchors the text to the entity origin (top/middle/bottom).
What text too big for its box does. Needs a layout box: Clip and Ellipsis drop the lines past its height and trim a line past its width; Shrink sets the text smaller until it fits both.

Draw layer for a text standing in the WORLD (no UINode) — read like Sprite/ShapeRenderer layer, so a label can sit in front of the content around it. Ignored inside a Canvas, where the UI render order decides.
Layout box width for a text with no UINode (0 = no box: the origin is the box). Alignment, wrapping and overflow work inside it. A UINode, if present, decides the box instead.
Layout box height (0 = none). Vertical alignment and Clip/Ellipsis need it.
Where the entity origin sits in the box, as a fraction from its left/bottom edge: (0.5, 0.5) is the centre, (0, 1) the top-left corner.
Translate the empty-field hint through the Localization resource. Leave empty for a literal placeholder.
A font file this project ships (.ttf / .otf). Overrides Font Family when set; leave empty to use a font the host already has.
A font the HOST already has (system or page-loaded). Ignored when Font is set.
Which characters the field accepts. Digits keeps only 0-9, whether typed or pasted, for a count or a price.
Where the value sits in the field. A single line holds the alignment while it fits, then scrolls to follow the caret.
Glyph pipeline for the field text — Auto (hinted bitmap when unscaled, SDF once scaled), always Bitmap, or always SDF.
The transform this camera orbits.
Upward speed a jump starts with. 0 = cannot jump.
Whose forward the stick is read against.
Grid layout: orthogonal, isometric, staggered, or hexagonal.
Hexagonal side length in px (0 = a regular pointy hex = tileHeight/2). Ignored unless orientation is Hexagonal.
Stagger axis (staggered/hex): Y shifts rows, X shifts columns.
Which lines carry the half-cell shift (staggered/hex).
Layer transparency (0 = invisible, 1 = opaque).
Override the clip's own wrap mode: once, loop or pingPong. Empty uses what the clip declares.
Clip completed (runtime, read-only). Raise Playing to replay.
Seconds each trail point lives before it fades out of the tail.
Min world distance moved before a new trail point is recorded.
Record new points. False = freeze and let the streak fade in place.
Full ribbon width at the head (newest point).
Full ribbon width at the tail (oldest point).
Color at the head (newest point).
Color at the tail (oldest point) — usually alpha 0 to fade out.
Blend mode: 0 Normal, 1 Additive (glow), 2 Multiply, …
Sorting layer — controls draw order across renderables.
Local position in world units, relative to the parent.
Local rotation in degrees, applied X then Y then Z. 2D content turns about Z alone.
Local scale per axis (1 = original size; negative flips).
Stencil only: above 0, clip to the mask sprite's shape instead of its box.
None removes this node and its whole subtree from layout, rendering and input.
Subtree opacity, multiplied down the tree. Fades this node and everything under it.
None makes this node and its subtree transparent to the pointer — hits pass through to what is behind.
The child that scrolls inside this node. Leave empty to use the first child.
Clamped stops at the ends; Elastic overshoots and springs back.
Fraction of flick velocity kept per second. 0 stops on release.
Let a click turn the selected toggle off, leaving none selected.
How the image fits its box: Fill stretches, Contain letterboxes it whole, Cover fills and crops.
An ocean is without edge: everywhere at its height where the ground is lower; a lake is a rectangle or an outline of its own; a river follows the Spline on the same entity.
What the game calls this body, the same in every session: what a query names the water by. Empty is named by its entity.
A lake's size along x.
A lake's size along z.
The outline of a lake: points round it on its own xz plane. Empty is the rectangle of its size.
How far in from the shore, and how deep, the waves take to come to full height. 0 leaves them whole to the edge.
A river's current, in world units a second where it is as wide as its widest. A narrower reach runs faster.
The height of the tallest wave, in world units. Their length, speed and heading are the zone's.
How deep the river cuts its bed into the terrain under its surface, at its middle, its banks blending back into the ground. 0 leaves the ground as it is.
The region baked along x, centred on the entity. Water outside it is not drawn; an ocean goes on past it.
The region baked along z, centred on the entity.
Texels along the longer side of the region: how finely shores and rivers are traced.
A material on the Water shader for the whole surface. Empty uses the stock water.
The length of the longest wave. Every body shares the waves; each sets how high they stand.
A multiplier on how fast the waves travel.
The heading of the waves, in degrees.
How high the surf breaking on a shore stands against its body's waves. 0 draws none. A current carries none.
The length of the surf's waves, in world units. They run in over four lengths of water, break, and run up the ground past the shore.
The cell size of the finest ring of the surface. Waves shorter than six cells are not drawn as geometry there (the shading still shows them).
Cells along a ring's side.
Rings of the surface, each twice as coarse as the one inside it.
Cells along a side of the grid that keeps what disturbs the water: bodies moving in it, rain, and what a script disturbs. 0 keeps none.
The side of the window the ripples are kept in, in world units. It follows the camera.
How fast a ripple spreads, in world units a second.
How much of its height a ripple loses each second.
How fast the foam a disturbance leaves fades, a second.
Where the joint attaches on the connected body, in that body's frame (pixels).
Where it attaches on this entity, in its own frame (pixels).
Direction of travel, in the connected body's frame.
The rules the world is laid out by: a .esworld file, or the id of rules the game registered with registerWorldRules.
The version of the rules the world was made with. A version the rules no longer have fails the world rather than laying out another one.
The world (a planet, a level) as the game names it.
Another seed lays out another world by the same rules.
Whether the biomes paint the terrain.
Plane: laid out over a Terrain. Planet: this entity is also a Planet, and the world is laid out over its six faces.
The height of the sea above the planet's radius: ground lower than this is under water.
Cells this close are prepared, not shown.
Cells this close are brought in.
Resident cells are kept until past this.
What the zone is for (home, road, landing, building, resource, view): the game's own words.
The circle's radius, in world units.
The box's size along its own x.
The box's size along its own z.
Over how many world units past the outline the zone fades out: what it keeps out thins there.
Where zones overlap, the higher priority holds the biome.
The tags of what the zone keeps out, separated by commas (a layer, a recipe, its tags, decor, interactive); * keeps out everything; empty keeps nothing out.
A biome the zone holds over its area; empty holds none.
Level the terrain under the zone to the ground's height at its centre, blending back over its falloff: a plot to build on.
